This manual is the primary reference document for Appeals & Grievances Coordinators on the Member Services team at Mojave Crest Assurance Company (MCA). Mojave Crest Assurance Company is a regional health insurer headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada. MCA writes fully insured commercial health, dental, and vision products in Nevada and is licensed and regulated by the Nevada Division of Insurance. 3.1 Product Structure

The Vista Access PPO is Mojave Crest's fully insured small group (2–50 eligible employees) commercial health plan. It is a preferred provider organiza3on, meaning members have access to both in-network and out-of-network benefits, with richer cost sharing in-network. The plan year runs on a calendar year basis for most groups, but individual employer groups may renew on other dates. Always confirm the plan year the claim falls under before looking up benefit details, because benefit structures can change year over year.

Vista Access integrates medical, behavioral health, and prescrip3on drug coverage. There is no behavioral health carve out as MCA is the payer for all three. This is important for parity analysis (see Sec3on 8) because it means Vista Access is subject to the full parity comparison between medical/surgical and mental health/substance use disorder benefits, with no separate vendor to point at.

4.2 Appeal vs. Grievance

Appeals and grievances are different processes with different 3melines and outcomes. . An appeal is a formal request to overturn an adverse benefit determina3on. An adverse benefit determina3on is any denial, reduc3on, or termina3on of a benefit. For example, a denied prior authoriza3on, a denied claim, a reduc3on in authorized units for physical therapy, or termina3on of ongoing authorized care. An appeal is asking MCA to change a decision. Appeals follow strict regulatory 3melines and result in a formal determina3on leQer with external review rights.

A grievance is a complaint about the quality of service, the behavior of MCA staff, the accessibility of the provider network, the clarity of plan documents, or any other dissa3sfac3on that does not involve a request to overturn a benefit decision. Grievances do not have the same regulatory clock as appeals and do not result in a determina3on leQer with external review rights. Grievances are logged, inves3gated, acknowledged, and responded to, but they do not change a benefit decision.

Here is the test you should apply at intake: does the member want MCA to approve, pay for, or authorize something that was previously denied, reduced, or terminated? If so, it is an appeal. If not, it is a grievance.

Mixed requests. A single leQer from a member can contain both an appeal and a grievance. The denial por3on is an appeal, while the rudeness complaint is a grievance. When this happens, open two separate cases, one appeal, and one grievance, with two dis3nct Case IDs. Each has its own clock and its own response process. Do not try to handle both in a single case file.

Vista Access recognizes five types of appeals. Each has its own 3meline rule and procedural requirements. Classify the appeal correctly at intake as a classifica3on error almost always produces a 3meline error.

4.3.1 Pre-Service Standard Appeal

A pre-service appeal is an appeal of a denied request for authoriza3on of care that has not yet been received. The classic example is a denied prior authoriza3on for an upcoming surgery, imaging study, or course of outpa3ent therapy. The service has not happened yet, and the member is dispu3ng the denial before receiving care. 4.3.2 Pre-Service Expedited Appeal

Expedited status is triggered either automa3cally (when the trea3ng physician cer3fies that expedited review is medically necessary) or by request (from the member, AOR, or provider) followed by MCA confirma3on that expedited criteria are met.

When a trea3ng physician cer3fies in wri3ng that expedited review is medically necessary, MCA must honor the request and proceed on the expedited 3meline. 14. Concurrent care appeals are always treated as expedited if the reduc3on or termina3on would end coverage before the appeal can be decided on within the standard 3meline.

A member's leQer is dated January 3, postmarked January 5, and arrives in the MCA mail room on January 8 — where it is scanned and uploaded to the appeals queue on January 9.
